spans.text: ...In the abandoned theater.
Sorry for the wait, people out there watching this stream!
We have now arrived at our destination—
The haunted theater!
Keep the views and likes coming if you're interested!
...I get that the theater is abandoned and all, but they didn't have to leave these puppets lying around like this, right?
They give me the creeps when it's so dark...
I-I can't shake the feeling that somebody is watching me...
MDR, what did this Jane Doe do afterwards?
Oh, right! Let's continue with the ghost story.
So our beautiful and talented Miss Passadou's life at the theater, which had been going swimmingly so far, was ruined.
She was tormented by her incurable illness and the betrayal of her love...
Meanwhile, like many clichéd novels, we have a villain – Jane Doe, who is deeply envious of Miss Passadou and seeks to completely replace her.
The easiest way of replacing someone is...
To become this person and eliminate her existence.
Wait, what exactly does that mean?
In Jane Doe's case, since she wished to replace Miss Passadou, she would wear Miss Passadou's face, take everything that belonged to Miss Passadou, then kill her.
...Was she deliberately re-enacting the story of "Butterfly in a Cocoon"?

It's apparent from Miss Jane Doe's actions that she adored Miss Passadou – she adored her so much she wanted to become her. It's hardly surprising that she would fashion her crime after Miss Passadou's most famous work.
Well, there's no definite psychoanalysis on Miss Jane Doe.
"All the world's a stage."
As Miss Passadou's most famous work, "Butterfly in a Cocoon" is a perfect caricature of her experience.
Are humans capable of completely replicating a person's face? Is that even legal?

As far as I know, it is only illegal for a Doll to bear close physical resemblance to an existing human, but there is no law that forbids a human from cosmetically altering their appearance based on another human's face.
Besides, humans have very advanced technology when it comes to cosmetic surgery, though I suppose it's still harder for them to change the way they look compared to us? I'm not too sure either.
In any case, this Jane Doe found a clinic that was willing to give her Miss Passadou's face, and she underwent the operation.
I have a question – unlike Dolls, wouldn't it take a human a long time to recuperate after undergoing such a radical facial reconstructive surgery?
And this is assuming that the surgery was even successful in the first place. From what I know, this kind of face replacement surgery has an extremely low rate of success.
That's right, she wouldn't be able to work at the theater while she was recovering from the operation.
Her boss would've totally ditched her if she was away for so long...
Who knows? Perhaps like the doppelgänger in the play, Miss Jane Doe also has special powers?
Anyway, by the time she returned to the theater, she was already the spitting image of Miss Passadou!
Even the staff had trouble telling them apart.
I have another question – I just ran a search in the database but there is no record of any woman named Jane Doe.
That's the freakiest thing about the story!
Among the survivors of the fire, not a single one remembered a woman called Jane Doe.
The police only learned of her through Miss Passadou's diary, but they couldn't find any other information about this woman, so nobody knows for sure if there was ever a Jane Doe.
In other words, Miss Jane Doe could've merely been a figment of Miss Passadou's imagination, or she could be an actual being that existed, just like the doppelgänger...
It's totally like "Butterfly in a Cocoon", but in reality...
This makes no sense at all.
I'll admit it does sound a bit dubious... But if it were entirely logical, it wouldn't have been much of an urban legend, would it?
Did you guys just hear something?
Hear what?
MDR hops onto the stage and presents it to the livestream camera with great gusto.
You see this, my friends? This is where Miss Passadou used to perform when she was alive!
Now don't be hasty, I'll show you around!
If you're enjoying this stream, remember to smash that subscribe button! Muah! ❤
Hey, MDR, I don't think it's a good idea to mess with the stuff in here...
She's right...
Don't sweat it! The place is deserted anyway!
I wonder if this piano even works...
MDR walks over to the old and battered piano in the corner. She lifts the lid and randomly pushes a key.
A gust of chilly wind blows through the auditorium.
In the blink of an eye, the charred theater is completely restored to its previous splendor.
The curtains slowly rises, revealing an empty stage.
Hey, what the hell did you do?!
What's going on? Are we in a different place?
Go easy on my arm, Miss MDR!
That's...
A graceful woman walks out onto the stage from the wing, delicate and colorful petals swirling gently around her.
Who's that?
She's lovely...
Hold on! Isn't that—
"Think of me, think of me fondly..."
"When we've said goodbye."
MDR, explain!
Miss MDR! Miss MDR, what's the matter with you?
MDR trembles silently, as if she had taken a heavy blow.
"Remember me, once in a while..."
"Please promise me you'll try."
That's Miss Passadou.
WHAAAT?!
But isn't she supposed to be...
"When you find..."
"That once again you long to take your heart back and be free..."
"If you ever find a moment..."
"Spare a thought for me."
The empty auditorium erupts in fervent applause.
AAAAAAAAAHHHHH! It's actually haunted!!!!
Leg it!!!
Miss 97S! That's a wall!
AAAAHHHH! Help!!!
Miss MDR!
...Have you never seen a hologram?
Spitfire frowns and makes her way over to Passadou, who is singing passionately...and walks right through her.
Stop dashing about like crazy bulls. It's just a projection.
All of a sudden, the scene around them shifts again.
Spitfire can even feel a warm and fragrant breeze blowing in her face.
Passadou lifts her skirts and walks into the flowerbed.
The hemline of her dress brushes against the small, delicate flowers as morning dew clings onto the fabric.
...Do you know who my idol is?
N-no.
Holyyyy crap... The ghost is talking to me!
AAAAAHHHH! RUN!!!
It's Eva Friedel, once known as the "Diva of the Century".
She was an opera singer, so not exactly like me, but she's still someone I want to become.
One day, I will also live on in people's memory as a Diva.
Even when my body is no more, my spirit will endure for eternity.
Eva Friedel, huh?
Until that day, you will always be with me, won't you?
Passadou smiles dazzlingly at the Dolls.
Type 97S' eyes roll back into her head and she collapses like a felled log.
AAAAAAH! LET ME OUTTA HERE!
(Sighs) Looks like these two won't chill until we shut down this holographic projection...
Is there anything I can do to help?
Good. Keep an eye on the surroundings for me, SASS.
I'm hacking the control system to see who's behind this.
No problem, leave it to me!
